stories.title: New plastic packaging chemicals linked to health risks
stories.summary: Exposure to Dinch, a chemical marketed as a high safety and nontoxic alternative to phthalates in food packaging, is linked to lower birth weight and fetal development complications. A new peer-reviewed study suggests the industry-touted replacement may not be as safe as claimed.

stories.title: Kataka seizes 150 kg of banned plastic
stories.summary: The Kataka Municipal Corporation seized 1.5 quintals of prohibited single-use plastic during a city-wide enforcement drive on Friday. The civic body urged residents and traders to switch to eco-friendly alternatives to help make the city cleaner, greener and more sustainable.

stories.title: Sikkim authorities seize 1.2 kg of banned plastic
stories.summary: Authorities confiscated 1.2 kg of prohibited single-use plastic items and collected 2,000 rupees in fines during inspections across seven municipal areas in Sikkim on November 3. Officials briefed shopkeepers on the Plastic Waste Management Rules, 2016, which include bans on items like plastic-stick ear buds.

stories.summary: The Food Safety and Standards Authority of India has proposed allowing chemically recycled polyethylene and polypropylene in food packaging. Manufacturers must ensure the recycled material meets virgin plastic safety standards. The proposal also allows recycled content in the outermost layer of multilayer packaging, provided barriers prevent chemical migration.

stories.title: John Hartwig wins 2026 Eni Award
stories.summary: Professor John F. Hartwig received the Advanced Environmental Solutions Award for his work on circular plastics recycling. His group developed a catalytic process to deconstruct polyethylene and polypropylene into monomer building blocks for reuse. The process aims to reduce waste and fossil-based raw material dependence without performance loss.

stories.title: Chemical process turns plastic waste into industrial adhesives
stories.summary: Researchers have developed a chemical process using solvents and light-activated reactions to transform polyethylene and polypropylene packaging into industrial-grade adhesives. The technique aims to provide a high-value alternative to traditional recycling methods, which often degrade the quality of plastic materials during the deconstruction process.

stories.title: Biffa reopens Suffolk facility after upgrade
stories.summary: Biffa has reopened its Masons materials recovery facility near Ipswich following a 12 million pound upgrade. The project, which adds glass processing capacity and advanced sorting technology, was funded by Biffa and the Packaging Extended Producer Responsibility scheme. The full piece is for subscribers.

stories.title: Nylene to incorporate recycled caprolactam
stories.summary: NylaNova has partnered with nylon producer Nylene to supply recycled caprolactam. The process converts nylon-6 waste into high-purity material with a reported 90 percent yield. NylaNova claims its green caprolactam produces 95 percent lower greenhouse gas emissions than traditional methods and remains competitively priced for the North American market.

stories.title: Abundia provides update on Texas facility
stories.summary: Abundia Global Impact Group has provided an update on its waste plastics-to-renewable fuels facility in Cedar Port, Texas. The company is using Topsoe’s HydroFlex technology for the project. Abundia reports that its partner has met all engineering deliverables due to date for the planned facility.

stories.title: The evolution of food-grade polypropylene recycling
stories.summary: Professor Edward Kosior, a 2020 Sustainability Awards winner, continues work on the NEXTLOOPP project. The initiative aims to create food-grade packaging from recycled polypropylene, a polymer that previously could not be returned to food contact products. The sector is now preparing for the 2026 Sustainability Awards.

stories.title: SMX highlights the economics of plastic recycling
stories.summary: SMX says the economics of plastic have turned recycling from an act of corporate responsibility into a financial imperative. The company provides authentication and traceability technology to help firms protect margins against volatile oil prices and plastic taxes. Recycling is now about controlling costs, not just protection.

stories.title: LIKAT explores new method for upcycling polyethylene
stories.summary: Chemists at LIKAT are developing a method to convert polyethylene into dicarboxylic acids for use as nylon precursors. The reaction proceeds under mild conditions without a catalyst. The team aims to scale the process to a pilot plant level to reduce reliance on petroleum-based nylon production.

stories.title: Study models PVC waste impact in China
stories.summary: A study covering 31 Chinese provinces from 2020 to 2050 suggests that waste management strategies will significantly impact the nation's carbon footprint. Researchers found that mechanical recycling currently delivers the lowest environmental footprint of any treatment option for polyvinyl chloride waste compared to landfill or incineration routes.

stories.title: Researchers develop adhesive from plastic waste
stories.summary: ETH Zurich researchers have created a one-step chemical process to transform polyethylene and polypropylene into high-performance adhesives. The technique attaches new polymer chains to the material instead of breaking it down. This approach aims to address the quality degradation often associated with conventional plastic recycling methods.

stories.title: Biffa completes Masons facility transformation
stories.summary: Biffa has reopened its Masons materials recovery facility after a 12 million pound upgrade. The project, funded by Biffa and the Packaging Extended Producer Responsibility scheme, adds glass processing and sorting technology. The facility aims to support higher-quality recycling infrastructure across the Suffolk and Braintree districts.

stories.title: Aduro completes 120-hour pilot campaign
stories.summary: Aduro Clean Technologies completed a 120-hour pilot plant campaign, its longest to date. The facility processed post-consumer plastic waste while testing feedstock changes and operating continuity. The company reports the pilot remained operational through a power outage during the testing period.

stories.title: EU packaging policy report
stories.summary: The PPWR has been the subject of significant political debate within the European Union. Market reports provide insight into how environmental directives are being interpreted and where pitfalls exist for member states. The full piece is for subscribers.

stories.title: California SB 54 and packaging costs
stories.summary: California's Senate Bill 54 is introducing extended producer responsibility fees and source-reduction targets. While industry focus has largely remained on primary packaging, the legislation places a new financial value on material consumption. The full piece is for subscribers.

stories.title: CalRecycle updates source reduction baseline
stories.summary: CalRecycle has updated its source reduction baseline for Senate Bill 54, which takes effect January 1, 2027. Producers must achieve 25 percent weight reductions in plastic packaging by 2032. The update is informed by data reported by producers to the state's chosen producer responsibility organization.

stories.title: California SB 54 data requirements
stories.summary: While California lawmakers have discussed delaying certain fees under Senate Bill 54, the law's data collection requirements remain in place. Businesses are currently navigating the assembly and reporting of extensive packaging material data, which is considered one of the legislation's most consequential features.

stories.title: Pakistan official calls for national EPR framework
stories.summary: Minister of State for Climate Change Dr Shezra Mansab Ali Khan Kharal has urged the government and private sector to develop a coordinated national framework for Extended Producer Responsibility. She said Pakistan needs to overhaul its waste management system and move towards a circular economy to curb pollution.

stories.title: Krones launches compact beverage packer
stories.summary: Krones has launched a compact Varioline 1M packer that reverses crate flow by 180 degrees without sacrificing production speed. The machine handles up to 103,000 containers per hour, using synchronized robotic handling to reduce bottle scuffing and noise. Germany’s Krombacher Brauerei has ordered the first two units.

stories.title: India pharmaceutical blister machine market analysis
stories.summary: India is a substantial pharmaceutical packaging equipment market where blister machines are purchased as part of a validated workflow. Thermoforming represents 60 to 75 percent of demand, while cold-forming lines serve products requiring higher barrier protection. Machines are rarely treated as stand-alone commodity items.

stories.title: India flap gluing machine market forecast
stories.summary: India’s flap gluing machine market relies on corrugated box production for the majority of its demand. The segment is expected to grow 6 to 9 percent annually through 2035 as e-commerce and industrial goods drive the need for reliable carton closure. Technical niches remain small.

stories.title: Japan bubble wrap machine market overview
stories.summary: Japan’s bubble wrap machine market includes film extrusion lines and on-demand converting systems. Equipment costs range from 300,000 yen for compact units to over 100 million yen for industrial extrusion lines. Domestic engineering is meaningful, though some components are sourced from specialized global suppliers.

stories.title: Packaging automation market to reach 126 billion dollars
stories.summary: The packaging automation industry is moving toward connected production systems that coordinate handling, inspection, and palletizing. Manufacturers are shifting investment priorities to address labor availability and shorter production schedules. The market is projected to reach 126.18 billion dollars by 2033 as individual machines become integrated systems.

stories.title: Corner and edge protection market trends
stories.summary: The global corner and edge protection market enters 2026 with more disciplined procurement and a diversified supply architecture. These components, made from materials including foam, metal, and paperboard, are used to prevent damage during transit. Demand fundamentals are described as broader than in previous years.

stories.title: India molded fiber egg packaging market
stories.summary: India’s molded fiber egg packaging market is locally supplied and freight-sensitive. Filler flats and bulk cases account for 40 to 55 percent of demand, while retail cartons represent 35 to 50 percent. Prices for a 30-egg flat range from 4 to 10 rupees before freight costs.

stories.title: Blister card packaging market evolution
stories.summary: The global blister card packaging market is shifting toward higher-barrier and automation-ready formats. Pre-formed plastic cavities remain a preferred solution for product visibility and tamper evidence. The market enters 2026 with a focus on sustainability compliance and a more regionally diversified supply architecture.

stories.title: Germany reusable consumer packaging market
stories.summary: Germany’s reusable packaging market includes deposit beverage containers and returnable grocery crates. Beverage reuse remains the most established model, while other categories face challenges with collection and reverse logistics. Demand is expected to expand 5 to 9 percent annually through 2035, driven by regulation and cost pressure.

stories.title: Hot fill packaging market to reach 16.5 billion dollars
stories.summary: The global hot fill packaging market was valued at 12.2 billion dollars in 2025. It is expected to grow at a 3.4 percent annual rate to reach 16.5 billion dollars by 2034. Adoption is increasing as food and beverage companies seek convenient, shelf-stable product formats.

stories.title: Beverage cups market undergoes structural realignment
stories.summary: The global beverage cups market is bifurcating into high-performance recyclable single-use cups and reusable systems. Regulatory pressure and channel consolidation are redefining competition in what was once a monolithic commodity space. The market enters 2026 with a focus on leasing, tracking, and washing infrastructure.

stories.title: Bulk packaging materials market growth
stories.summary: The global bulk packaging materials market provides large-capacity containers for loose and granular goods. As of 2026, the market is shaped by persistent demand from emerging economies and regulatory pressure for circular economy practices. Supply architecture is becoming more regionally diversified to support industrial logistics.

stories.title: Clamshell packaging market dynamics
stories.summary: The global clamshell packaging market is a mature segment balancing e-commerce growth with safety regulations. The two-shell hinged design is used for product visibility and tamper resistance. The market enters 2026 with more disciplined procurement behavior and a focus on conflicting forces of presentation and safety.

stories.title: Raj Packaging Industries reports profit increase
stories.summary: Raj Packaging Industries reported a net profit of 33.47 lakh rupees for the second quarter of fiscal year 2027, a 13-fold increase year-on-year. Revenue grew 37.46 percent to 1,140.11 lakh rupees. The board approved a 985.30 lakh rupee capital expenditure funded by loans and internal accruals.

stories.title: Shri Techtex revenue rises 146 percent
stories.summary: Shri Techtex reported first-half fiscal year 2027 revenue of 90.92 crore rupees, a 146 percent increase year-on-year. Net profit rose 130 percent to 13.90 crore rupees, while the net profit margin declined to 15.3 percent. Rising polymer prices and freight pass-through contributed to the revenue growth.

stories.title: Shri Techtex margins compress despite revenue growth
stories.summary: Shri Techtex reported first-half fiscal year 2027 revenue of 90.92 crore rupees, up 146 percent year-on-year. Net profit rose 130 percent to 13.90 crore rupees, but the EBITDA margin fell to 22.3 percent from 26.8 percent. Costs for materials and traded goods rose to 65.3 percent of revenue.

stories.title: Ardagh Group seeks to sell metal can business
stories.summary: Ardagh Group is seeking to divest its metal can business to focus on glass packaging. The move adds uncertainty for beverage brands already dealing with limited can availability. Supply challenges have not eased enough to remove market pressure, even as demand for cans remains high.

stories.title: Rakuten Investment Management acquires Amcor shares
stories.summary: Rakuten Investment Management purchased 82,986 shares of Amcor for 3.52 million dollars in the third quarter. Amcor reported quarterly revenue of 6.13 billion dollars, exceeding consensus estimates. The company raised its quarterly dividend to 0.66 dollars per share, resulting in a stated yield of about 5.9 percent.

stories.title: Pyramid Technoplast earnings call recordings available
stories.summary: Pyramid Technoplast filed a disclosure confirming that audio and video recordings of its earnings conference call for the quarter and half-year ended 30 September 2026 are available on its website. The call with analysts and investors took place on 06 November 2026.

stories.title: Shri Jagdamba Polymers reports profit growth
stories.summary: Shri Jagdamba Polymers reported a 54.1 percent rise in net profit to Rs 35.66 crore for the half year ended 30 September 2026. Revenue from operations grew 37.6 percent to Rs 345.59 crore. Trade receivables also rose to Rs 168.07 crore during the same period.

stories.title: Shri Jagdamba Polymers working capital reaches 202 crore
stories.summary: Shri Jagdamba Polymers reported core working capital of 202 crore at 30 September 2026, up from 133.3 crore at 31 March 2026. Trade receivables increased by 53.56 crore and inventories rose by 22.89 crore. Net debt climbed to 47.52 crore as cash and equivalents declined.

stories.title: Newman Foods secures 3 million dollar loan for expansion
stories.summary: Ugandan agro-processing company Newman Foods has secured a 2.93 million dollar mezzanine loan from AgDevCo Ventures. The company plans to use the funds to expand processing capacity and increase purchases from its network of 3,000 smallholder farmers. The firm aims to meet rising demand for local products.

stories.title: Cosmo First reports Q2 results
stories.summary: Cosmo First reported improved EBITDA for the quarter ended September 2026, citing 15 percent higher sales volume and a reduction in US tariffs. Results included a 24.8 crore duty refund and a 7 crore stock loss from falling raw material prices. The company is currently evaluating tax options.

stories.title: Ester Industries reports revenue growth
stories.summary: Ester Industries reported consolidated income of 449.0 crore for the second quarter of fiscal year 2027, up from 357.2 crore in the same period last year. EBITDA reached 45.1 crore compared to 17.3 crore previously. Profit after tax rose to 7.8 crore from a loss of 15 crore.

stories.title: JK Paper completes corporate restructuring
stories.summary: JK Paper Limited has completed a restructuring scheme involving the amalgamation of three subsidiaries and demerger operations. The company allotted 1.19 crore equity shares to shareholders of Enviro Tech Ventures Limited. This move increases the total paid up capital of the firm to 181.32 crore.
